name: Processor Design Laboratory
description: This is a course covering the design and implementation of modern computing systems, spanning microarchitectural building blocks of high-performance processors and domain-specific accelerators. Topics include branch predictors, instruction fetch logic, decode and rename logic, instruction window and scheduler, select logic, load-store queue, ALUs and bypass paths, instruction commit logic, misprediction and recovery techniques, and selective replay techniques. The course also teaches how to express compute kernels in C++ and synthesise them to RTL using High Level Synthesis, apply optimisation directives for pipeline initiation interval, loop unrolling, and on-chip memory banking, integrate accelerators with a host processor via AXI interfaces, and evaluate throughput, area, and energy tradeoffs using roofline analysis and synthesis reports.
